answer: An agent may settle only after joining a mutual-insurance circle capped at twelve members and backed by a shared basalt bond that no member may reuse on a second name. Admission requires a short signed sonnet that hashes the applicant's keys and payout route; members countersign only when the wording and funding path look unique. Settled fees then rest in a velvet hold for two epochs, and any correlated default or reused oath slashes the bond. A farm of fake identities must either persuade genuine members to share that bond or fund many circles and still risk a group wipeout.
